questions.q: Who pushed Uqbah away when he tried to choke the Prophet SAW?
questions.explain: Abu Bakr bravely stood against injustice and was beaten.

questions.q: What title did the Prophet SAW give Abyssinia?
options: Ard as-Sidq, the land of truth
questions.explain: Abyssinia was chosen because it was outside Persian power and as a fallback.

questions.q: How many set out in the first migration to Abyssinia?
questions.explain: They left quietly and boarded ships at Shu'aybah.

questions.q: Why did Abu Bakr return Ibn Daghinah's protection?
options: Because he did not want protection to restrict his da'wah
The cave youths who fled to save their faith
questions.explain: Quraysh asked about them and Allah answered in Surah Al-Kahf.

questions.q: Those sent to Abyssinia were weak companions with no influence.
questions.explain: False. Those sent were strong and influential; migration is no sign of weakness.

questions.q: Umar was thought impossible to embrace Islam, yet the Prophet SAW still prayed for him.
questions.explain: True. Do not despair of anyone.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Abu Bakr cancels his migration and is protected
An-Nadr and Uqbah go to Yathrib
Al-Kahf and Al-Isra answer the questions

questions.explain: To Yathrib, revelation delayed, Al-Kahf answered, migration to Abyssinia, and Abu Bakr protected.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: A hadith with a weak chain but not fabricated
An onlooker who takes no side
The assembly hall of Makkah's leaders
A traveller told of in the Quran

questions.explain: A bystander is an onlooker, Dar an-Nadwah is Makkah's hall, Dhul-Qarnayn is a traveller in the Quran, and a daif hadith has a weak chain.

questions.q: What is the lesson when revelation was delayed after the Prophet SAW forgot to say insha-Allah?
options: Say insha-Allah and rely on Allah
questions.explain: The delay taught reliance on Allah.
